title.narrative: Strengthened social dialogue Institutions and evidence based compliance systems in line with ILS

description.narrative:
Mechanisms for social dialogue in Eswatini need to be streamlined to foster meaningful and effective tripartite engagement on economic, labour, and social policy issues, and to improve the governance of the labour market. The configuration and functions of the labour administration system with particular focus on the Ministry of Labour & Social Security need to be strengthened to ensure greater responsiveness to emerging needs of the labour market. The state of occupational health and safety as revealed by the National OSH Profile 2023 reveals the urgent need to improve OSH systems and infrastructure and responsiveness to gender.
The strategy focuses on policy advice, capacity building, training to support the Government of Eswatini and the Social Partners to institute reforms towards a suitable model of social dialogue engagement, support a comprehensive review of the labour administration system, support the holistic review of the industrial relations act, support efforts by dispute resolution and prevention institutions to strengthen their effectiveness in labour dispute prevention and resolution; and provide continued support towards strengthening the capacity and effectiveness of the labour inspectorate through strategic compliance approaches. To address the state of occupational health and safety, support is being provided to operationalize the National OSH Policy and to review the Occupational Health and Safety Act, bringing it in greater alignment with the OSH Policy and Conventions 155 (and P155) and 187. To strengthen the knowledge base and evidence-based policy planning, Government is also drawing upon ILO support to strengthen the collection of quality of labour market statistics by aligning the instruments used for the collection of labour force data with the latest statistical standards
